title: Ninety-four cents of every dollar
sub: Hyperscaler capital spending as a share of their operating cash flow - PIMCO's projection for the next two years
src: PIMCO, AI Credit Expansion: Assessing the Micro and Macro Risks, Figure 3 - a projection, not an actual
src_full: PIMCO, 'AI Credit Expansion: Assessing the Micro and Macro Risks', Figure 3: aggregate hyperscaler capex expected to absorb 94% of operating cash flow over the next two years. The PIMCO paper is not on disk; the figure is the dossier's record of it.

proof.quote: aggregate hyperscaler capex is expected to absorb **94% of operating cash flow** over the next two years (Figure 3).
| 5 | Hyperscaler capex 2026E $690B / 2027E $870B; 94% of OCF | our chart | PIMCO Fig. 2–3 | ✅ |
Over the next two years, PIMCO has this buildout consuming ninety-four percent of every dollar these companies generate from operations. Ninety-four.

provenance_note: P69 T14a (2026-09-22). The script's sentence is PIMCO's FORWARD claim (two years ahead, five hyperscalers, Figure 3), so this object draws only that. The OTHER 94 is a different claim and is not drawn here: ev-capex-funding-v1's mark '94 cents of every dollar - operating cash consumed, Q1 '26' is a realised single quarter from company filings aggregated by Epoch AI (148.4 / 157.9 = 94.0%, MSFT AMZN GOOGL META ORCL). They agree by coincidence of rounding, not by source. domain [0, 100] states the scale: the whole of operating cash flow, drawn as the rule.
